ABOUT THE FOUNDER

Cynthia Soto-Cardinault, PhD

Computational biologist specializing in multiomics data analysis, bioinformatics, and reproducible scientific workflows.

Explore full academic profile →

SCIENTIFIC PROFILE

Interdisciplinary research experience

My background combines computer science, molecular biology, and computational genomics. My research spans plant molecular biology and human neurogenomics, with a focus on transcriptomic, epigenomic, and spatial data analysis.

Plant molecular biology

During my PhD at the Centro de Investigación Científica de Yucatán (CICY), I investigated plant defense mechanisms using RNA-seq and gene co-expression network analysis.

Human neurogenomics

At the Lieber Institute for Brain Development, I contributed to research integrating single-nucleus RNA-seq, chromatin accessibility, and spatial transcriptomics to study the human brain.

SELECTED PUBLICATIONS

Scientific contributions

Multi-omic spatial mapping of the human habenula defines the molecular and anatomical organization of medial and lateral subregions — Montgomery KD et al., bioRxiv (2026), preprint.

Network Analysis of Publicly Available RNA-seq Provides Insights into the Molecular Mechanisms of Plant Defense against Multiple Fungal Pathogens in Arabidopsis thaliana — Soto-Cardinault C et al., Genes (2023).

DNA Methylation and Transcriptomic Next-Generation Technologies in Cereal Genomics — Soto-Cardinault CG et al., Methods in Molecular Biology (2020).
